Voices? No, I don't hear any voices. Just the normal stuff, you know, the radio chatter in my head sometimes after a long shift. We use these Motorola radios, and the static on the main dispatch channel is always so loud. You can turn the squelch down, but then you miss half of what central is saying. It wouldn't swipe to let me into the supply room anymore. 

The supply room is where they keep all the good trauma dressings, the big bulky ones. We go through those so fast on the weekends, especially when the bars close and people start fighting out on the street. I saw a guy get hit with a barstool once, completely shattered his jaw. They had to wire it shut for six weeks. I can't imagine having my jaw wired shut. You'd have to drink everything through a straw. I like milkshakes, but only if they're thick enough that you actually need a spoon. The diner near my apartment makes the best strawberry milkshakes. They use real strawberries, not that fake syrup stuff that tastes like cough medicine. I hate the taste of cherry cough syrup. It reminds me of being a kid and having strep throat. My mom used to try to hide it in orange juice, but you can always taste it. Orange juice is better with pulp anyway, it feels more real.

Unreasonable? No, it wasn't unreasonable at all, it was necessary. That's actually why they sent me here. At the station, I kept moving the airway bags into this pattern, a pattern I just knew was right. I had to do it. We used to make fruit punch in these massive orange coolers for the neighborhood block parties when I was growing up. Everyone on the street would bring a dish to share. Mrs. Gable next door always brought potato salad, but she put raisins in it. Who puts raisins in potato salad? It's completely wrong. Tulips are nice, but they only bloom for like two weeks in the spring and then the petals just fall off everywhere and make a mess on the mulch. It's this giant metal sculpture that looks like a crumpled up piece of tin foil. It's supposed to represent the flow of the river or something, but it's just blinding when the sun hits it. \n\nThe sun has been so brutal lately, anyway. The AC in the back of our rig is barely blowing cool air. I tried to put in a maintenance request for it, but the mechanics are always backed up. He eats these huge sub sandwiches for lunch while he's working on the engines, just getting mayo and oil all over the steering wheels. I can't stand mayonnaise. My mom used to make egg salad sandwiches for school lunches, and by the time noon rolled around, my whole locker smelled like sulfur. She tried every cream on the market, but nothing worked until she switched to cloth diapers. Cloth diapers seem like so much work, though. You have to wash them constantly, and the washing machine at her house is this ancient top-loader that sounds like a jet engine taking off during the spin cycle. Jet engines are incredibly loud, obviously. We had to do a standby at the airport once for a plane that blew a tire on landing, and the noise out on the tarmac was deafening. Even with those big foam ear muffs, you could feel the vibration in your chest. Vibrations always make my teeth ache, right in the back where my wisdom teeth used to be. I had them out when I was nineteen, and the oral surgeon gave me laughing gas. It didn't make me laugh, it just made my arms feel like they were floating away like balloons. Balloons are terrible for the environment, especially the Mylar ones. They get tangled up in power lines and cause outages. We had a call last summer where a transformer blew because of a foil balloon, and this whole neighborhood lost power for two days right in the middle of a heatwave. Tulips are nice, but they only bloom for like two weeks in the spring and then the petals just fall off everywhere and make a mess on the mulch. Mulch always smells so sour when it's fresh.\n\nDoctor: When you feel driven to repeat the numbers or arrange the bags, does it feel like the urge comes from your own mind and is unwanted?\n\nPatient: Unwanted? No, no, it's not unwanted. I have to do it. Like I said, that's the whole reason they made me come here. I was at the station, and I just had to keep moving the airway bags into this specific pattern. I knew it was the right pattern. And I was saying the dispatch numbers out loud while I did it, over and over. Miller, my lieutenant, he kept yelling at me to stop and step back, but I couldn't. If I broke the sequence, the whole bay was going to go bad. Everything would just be ruined. \n\nIt's like when you're stocking the rig at the beginning of a shift. You have to make sure everything is in the exact right spot. The IV lines, the flushes, the gauze. If you reach for a tourniquet and it's not in the side pocket where it belongs, you're scrambling, and seconds matter. I hate those new CAT tourniquets they bought us, though. The windlass rod feels cheap, like it's going to snap if you crank it too hard. They switched suppliers a few months ago to save money. The city is always trying to save a buck on our gear, but then they go and spend millions on a new art installation downtown. It's this giant metal sculpture that looks like a crumpled up piece of tin foil. It's supposed to represent the flow of the river or something, but it's just blinding when the sun hits it. \n\nThe sun has been so brutal lately, anyway. The AC in the back of our rig is barely blowing cool air. I tried to put in a maintenance request for it, but the mechanics are always backed up. They have this one mechanic, Gary, who works in the fleet garage. He always has grease under his fingernails. I don't think he ever really washes his hands. He eats these huge sub sandwiches for lunch while he's working on the engines, just getting mayo and oil all over the steering wheels. I can't stand mayonnaise. It's just eggs and oil whipped together, right? But it smells so sour if it sits out. My mom used to make egg salad sandwiches for school lunches, and by the time noon rolled around, my whole locker smelled like sulfur. Lockers in middle school were so small, I could barely fit my winter coat in mine. It was this puffy blue coat that made me look like a marshmallow. I hated that coat.\n\nDoctor: At any point, do you think the repeated bag-arranging and number-repeating is excessive or unreasonable?\n\nPatient: I feel like I just answered this. No, it wasn't excessive or unreasonable. Like I said, that's exactly why they sent me here in the first place. I was at the station, and I kept moving the airway bags into a pattern because I just knew it was right. I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud, and my lieutenant kept telling me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't do it. I couldn't stop. It felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence. \n\nThe bay is always so echoey anyway, especially when the big roll-up doors are shut. They grease the tracks on those doors with this thick industrial lubricant that smells exactly like black licorice. I can't stand black licorice. My grandfather used to eat those little black jellybeans, the ones everyone else leaves at the bottom of the Easter basket. Easter grass is the worst invention ever, by the way. It's just shredded plastic that gets stuck in the vacuum cleaner brush. Our vacuum at the station is completely broken right now because the probie tried to vacuum up a bunch of spilled kitty litter. We keep kitty litter in the bay to soak up oil spills under the rigs. Oil is so hard to get off your boots. If you step in it, you leave these little black footprints all over the linoleum in the break room, and then the captain loses his mind. He's very particular about the floors. He actually makes us mop with this pine solution that makes my eyes water. Pine trees always remind me of those little air fresheners people hang from their rearview mirrors. They don't even smell like real trees, just chemicals.\n\nDoctor: When you think the injury review people are watching you through the cameras, could you be mistaken about that?\n\nPatient: Mistaken? No, I'm not mistaken. I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. They keep changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe, even when they sit there and tell me it's just routine paperwork. They think I don't see it, but I know what I wrote. \n\nThey use those little dome cameras in the corners of the ceiling, the ones with the smoked glass so you can't tell which way the lens is pointing. They installed those last year when they upgraded the security system. The guy who put them in left a bunch of drywall dust on the floor in the hallway, and nobody bothered to sweep it up for a week. Drywall dust is so fine, it just gets into everything. It's like baby powder, but gritty. My sister used to use baby powder all the time when my nephew was born. He had the worst diaper rash. She tried every cream on the market, but nothing worked until she switched to cloth diapers. Cloth diapers seem like so much work, though. You have to wash them constantly, and the washing machine at her house is this ancient top-loader that sounds like a jet engine taking off during the spin cycle. Jet engines are incredibly loud, obviously. We had to do a standby at the airport once for a plane that blew a tire on landing, and the noise out on the tarmac was deafening. Even with those big foam ear muffs, you could feel the vibration in your chest. Vibrations always make my teeth ache, right in the back where my wisdom teeth used to be. I had them out when I was nineteen, and the oral surgeon gave me laughing gas. It didn't make me laugh, it just made my arms feel like they were floating away like balloons. Balloons are terrible for the environment, especially the Mylar ones. They get tangled up in power lines and cause outages. We had a call last summer where a transformer blew because of a foil balloon, and this whole neighborhood lost power for two days right in the middle of a heatwave. Heatwaves are miserable when you're stuck wearing dark blue uniform pants that don't breathe at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever think these camera and note changes might be a false belief or a mistake on your part?\n\nPatient: I feel like we are going in circles here. I literally just told you it is not a mistake. It is not a false belief. I know for an absolute fact that the injury review people and the supervisors are watching me on the station cameras. They are going in and changing my triage notes because they want to make me look unsafe. And they can sit there and tell me it is just routine paperwork all they want, but I know what is really happening. \n\nSpeaking of routine paperwork, they make us fill it out with these cheap blue pens. The ones where the caps always crack. My partner, Dave, he chews on his pen caps until they are just mangled pieces of plastic. It is completely disgusting. And when he is not chewing them, he clicks them. Click, click, click, the whole time we are sitting in the cab waiting for a dispatch. It drives me absolutely insane. It sounds exactly like the metronome my piano teacher used to use when I was a kid. Mrs. Higgins. She had this old wooden metronome that ticked so loud you could hear it out in her driveway. She lived in this massive Victorian house that always smelled like mothballs and peppermint. Peppermint is actually supposed to settle your stomach, you know. Whenever we get a patient in the back of the rig who is nauseous, I tell them to sniff an alcohol prep pad because it works just like peppermint. But a lot of people hate the smell of rubbing alcohol. They say it reminds them of hospitals. I don't really mind hospitals, but the lighting in the ER triage area is always so harsh. Those long fluorescent tubes give me a headache right behind my eyes. It is the exact same kind of headache you get when you eat ice cream too fast. Brain freeze. I actually haven't had ice cream in months. The soft serve machine at the dairy freeze down the street from the station has been broken since April. They claim it is a supply chain issue with the parts, but I am pretty sure the teenagers working there just don't want to clean it at night. Cleaning those machines takes forever because you have to take apart all those sticky little valves and O-rings.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever have other beliefs that seem very clearly true to you but that other people say are impossible or not real?\n\nPatient: I just... I know it's not. \n\nPaperwork is the bane of my existence anyway. We switched to this new electronic patient care reporting system last year, and the tablets they gave us are completely useless. The touch screens only work half the time, especially if you have gloves on. Nitrile gloves make your hands sweat so much in the summer. When you take them off, your hands look like you've been sitting in the bathtub for an hour. My mom used to make me take bubble baths when I was little, but she always bought this cheap off-brand bubble bath that smelled like fake strawberries. It didn't even make good bubbles, they would just pop after two seconds. You need the kind with glycerin to make the really big bubbles that last. Glycerin is actually a byproduct of making soap, I think. Or maybe it's biodiesel. Biodiesel smells like French fries when it burns. There's this guy in my neighborhood who converted an old Volkswagen Jetta to run on vegetable oil from the diner down the street. The diner has the best hash browns, they're always perfectly crispy on the edges. I like to put hot sauce on them, but only the green kind. The red kind has too much vinegar. Vinegar is great for cleaning windows, though. It doesn't leave streaks like the blue spray stuff does. The blue spray always leaves a film if you wipe it with paper towels instead of a microfiber cloth. Microfiber cloths are amazing because they pick up everything, but if you wash them with regular towels, they get covered in lint and they're basically ruined. Lint traps in dryers are huge fire hazards if you don't clean them out. We go to at least three dryer fires a year, usually in those big apartment complexes where people just shove their clothes in and walk away.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel driven to repeat the bag-arranging or number-repeating to relieve a feeling of tension or anxiety?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I mean, that's why they sent me here in the first place. My lieutenant kept telling me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't do it. I couldn't. It's just like when they salt the roads in the winter. The salt trucks always rust out so fast because the rock salt just eats right through the metal undercarriage. My dad had an old Chevy truck that rusted out completely around the wheel wells. He tried to patch it himself with fiberglass and Bondo, but Bondo smells so terrible when it's curing. It has this really sharp chemical odor that gets stuck in your nose. It's kind of like the smell of those heavy-duty bleach wipes we use to clean the stretcher mattresses. Those wipes dry out my hands so badly. I have to use this special lotion with colloidal oatmeal in it, but the smell of oatmeal always makes me think of those little packets of instant maple brown sugar oatmeal my mom made me before school. Maple syrup is impossible to clean up if you spill it. If you leave even a drop on the counter, it attracts ants instantly. Ants are incredibly organized, though. They follow those invisible pheromone trails for miles just to find one little crumb of sugar. Sugar is terrible for your teeth.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any period when you felt unusually energized or euphoric for several days in a row?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really get like that.
